correctness.rationale: Tree-incidence Gram determinants equal products of forest-component sizes, giving the exact facet areas and fixed volume. Prüfer/Cayley enumeration gives exact expected counts with a necessary half-factor at balanced cuts. Uniform Stirling bounds and an exact harmonic partial-fraction sum yield the stated leading coefficient with O(n^(3/2)) remainder. Fixed-size cut convergence and the unit-mass Borel progeny distribution imply the facet-area weak limit; its infinite mean is reconciled with logarithmically divergent finite-dimensional means. The included standard-library checker independently verified all 1,440 labeled trees on 3 through 6 vertices, each relevant Gram minor, exact finite expectations, and asymptotic consistency. The proof, not numeric extrapolation, controls arbitrary dimension.

originality.rationale: The assessed novel statement is the uniform-Cayley graphical-zonotope Euclidean surface expectation with its explicit sharp logarithmic coefficient and the facet-area Borel limit/nonuniform-integrability link. Primary graphical-zonotope deformation results, i.i.d.-random-zonotope valuation results, and established tree edge-division comparisons cover important inputs but do not state or logically yield this combined high-dimensional dependent-generator law without new Cayley cut averaging and uniform asymptotic analysis. Relevant mathematical-record searches and 115 accessible earlier own claims revealed no implication covering the stochastic theorem. Absolute bibliographic completeness is not asserted.
